analysis: Examined the ProviderLoop.swift changes. The new stored property operatorModelFilter is added at head lines ~221-224 and set in init at head line 946-948. It is the union of backend.enabledModels and the startup models, and nil when enabledModels is empty. The lines I could see were the init (units 6 and 7), but the property declaration and the code that reads the filter (operatorFilterAllows) are outside the supplied units. The filter is only a state seed here. Nothing in the visible text consumes it, so I cannot confirm how it gates desired_models or prefetch convergence, or whether it gates anything else. Open question for integration: when enabled_models is empty the filter is nil, which the doc comment says serves any coordinator-pushed model. That is pre-existing behavior, not introduced here, but the coordinator-trusted prefetch/load path should be confirmed to still honor autopilot selection (autopilotAllowsModel) and the advertised-set guard in ensureModelLoaded. Test changes (AutopilotInventoryTests.swift) only adjust the loop() helper to accept an enabledModels list. The successor test now includes the successor in the operator filter. This suggests production code in another file now refuses desired-build convergence outside the operator filter, which is a tightening. The assertion that the unrelated build is still disallowed is retained. MockCoordinator.swift adds a test-only pushPrefetchModel helper with no production surface. No concrete security regression was identified in the supplied units. Relevant threat IDs: TB-002 (coordinator to provider websocket), A-004 and T-027 (model substitution), A-018. The consumer of operatorModelFilter in unseen files (Prefetch/ModelLoading extensions) should be examined by the next pass.
